sentences.text: Bromsgroveia was a predatory archosaur that lived during the Middle Triassic in England.
This animal is classified within the class Reptilia.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a right ilium collected from Coton Green Quarry in Warwickshire.
In 1842, Owen incorrectly assigned the holotype to Labyrinthodon pachygnathus, believing it to be a large frog.
Galton named and described the species Bromsgroveia walkeri in 1985, classifying it within the Rauisuchia.
Additional remains including vertebrae and teeth found in the 1980s and 1990s were described by Galton and Walker in 1996.
Bromsgroveia is closely related to Ctenosauriscus and belongs to the family Ctenosauriscidae.
The pelvic girdle of Bromsgroveia links it to Ctenosauriscus, Lotosaurus, Arizonasaurus, and Hypselorhachis.
The parent group of Bromsgroveia is the family Ctenosauriscidae.
